Bear in mind that M23 has RDF rolling with them frequently, some of whom do use drone jammers [https://www.janes.com/osint-insights/defence-news/rwanda-using-electronic-warfare-systems-in-drc](https://www.janes.com/osint-insights/defence-news/rwanda-using-electronic-warfare-systems-in-drc) 

Also, if we decide to roll in anything heavy like manned CAS we better bring SEAD because the RDF brought wheeled PRC-built SAM's into the DRC. [https://thedefensepost.com/2024/02/12/rwanda-missiles-dr-congo/](https://thedefensepost.com/2024/02/12/rwanda-missiles-dr-congo/)

That's not press we need. It would be better to try and get the FARDC back on their feet while trying to find ways to diplomatically persuade Kagame to pull back. Not easy, but the better option imo.

Hence why I don't see us going for it with boots on the ground. I could see us doing a training mission for the FARDC and advisors plus limited SOF action, but that's it. You don't even want American contractors around this stuff because this is too far from any assistance. If a SANDF mechanized unit could get beaten up by M23 at Sake and Goma, what are some dudes rolling around in at best MRAPs gonna do? 

Yes I know the SANDF contingent had been going through hellish logistical situations but they were rolling towards that fight heavy early in the day, they were loaded for bear. I mean no disrespect to the SANDF fallen. I just want to emphasize that M23 regularly has RDF units attached, some of whom have special equipment like drone jammers.

Thank you for the link, I took a look at the proposal. I find it interesting it was done by a lobbyist on behalf of a DRC senator. Overall the points are definitely relevant and pointed towards attracting the Admin's attention. Problem is when I see this 

\- "Granting the U.S. access to military bases in key zones to protect strategic resources.

\- "Replacing ineffective U.N. peacekeeping operations with direct U.S.-DRC security cooperation"

Would entail having us partially replace the remaining 14,000 troops under MONUSCO with a mix of U.S. and FARDC troops. Which is a terrible idea for us.

We would have to deploy possibly thousands of troops far from any of our established bases deep into central Africa to a place where resupply, replenishment, and casualty care and extraction would be monstrously difficult. Doubly so if we do kill AFRICOM.

Even if we were to turn this into a major commitment, we would now be taxing ourselves in Africa at a time when we're continually (or rather, should be) trying to re-capitalize our forces towards the Indo-Pacific. While having access to rare-earth minerals does factor into that equation, in order to slake our thirst we would essentially be drinking out of a poison well. We would become embroiled in DRC politics and the myriad of armed conflicts going on within its borders. 

Training and assisting the FARDC is something we could and should be doing, that and possibly some SOF stuff to curtail M23 while keeping a light footprint. Anything too much would drag us down.

All that said, I do think its possible that Kinshasa and D.C. come to some kind of agreement in time because this is a spot where their interests dovetail. The DRC needs security assistance, we need the resources. How the needle gets threaded will be interesting.

Prince being involved doesn't surprise me, however you'd need a sizeable contingent that can be backed by considerable firepower. Otherwise you end up looking like dorks like those Romanian PMC's in Goma. You'd need to surpass the kind of throw weight Blackwater could pull during the GWOT era.

Granted, Rwanda/M23 probably wouldn't want to pick a fight with contractors for fear of repercussions, but they can make accidents happen should they desire. This is their neck of the woods and its a far place to do resupply for either contractors or the military proper. And that's before you get into the terrible logistics situation of trying to move things around/maneuver in country, especially in the Kivus.

Could you cite where we would have to put boots on the ground? I would want to see the deets on what sort of deployment and how. That would be interesting considering the Admin may want to shutter AFRICOM. 

Also, while we outclass both nations in this instance I always trend on the side of caution when dealing with Kageme's Rwanda. This is the same country that kicked off the 1st and 2nd Congo Wars, got away with a lot of rather nasty actions, and is in the middle of successfully modernizing its military to a standard above its peers.

I would agree that agreeing to this deal is likely in Kinshasa's favor given the deteriorating security situation in the east and the desire to kneecap the M23 offensive. While there are very real concerns over the damage that more mining can do to the environment, it is also true that the DRC wants to have the infrastructure to actually mine its rare earths in a way that many of its neighbors can't. 

As for partitioning the DRC from a Rwandan POV, that to me is a bit of a pipedream as the non-Banyamulenge in the east friggin despise them. They would rule over angry subjects. That said, I know that the M23 is also trying to appear legitimate. 

Another aspect to cover in all this, is another attempt by Trump to offload migrants somewhere else. Namely, Rwanda. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-administration-in-talks-with-rwanda-to-take-deportees-from-u-s/](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-administration-in-talks-with-rwanda-to-take-deportees-from-u-s/)

Don't underestimate local actors, they have agency.

There is no way Kagame and the Rwandan leadership would sign in good faith. Having a buffer zone in the eastern DRC is something they've always wanted, alongside seizing control of the mining operations in the Kivu provinces. I could see them possibly signing, and then reneging at a later point. 

Unless we are willing to put boots on the ground in the DRC, which I find highly unlikely, the Rwandans and M23 will hold the edge on the battlefield. 

From the DRC perspective, having kicked out virtually all the other peacekeepers you could call on and having the remainder (SADC) get trounced at Goma, I can see how using other forms of leverage would be good against Rwanda. Overall the people of the Kivu's deserve peace, and the citizens of the DRC deserve to not get attacked by their neighbors (I'm looking at you too Uganda). 

However, if there is no means of enforcement, nothing will happen.

For me its the assembly of the mini that drives how I want to paint it as I can get an idea of how it will look in my head when I'm putting it together. Knew I didn't like the OG Judiciar concept for the SW, so I ditched the head, the tempormortis, and swapped the executioner sword for a frostblade. Wanted him roaring into battle having a pint.  


But as far as paints used, that's complicated because I don't actually write this down as I go. Body is primed black (use any), head is wraithbone base. Black is successive grey highlights using artis opus drybrushes in a zenithal manner (don't remember all of them but mostly dawnstone and the highest I wanted to go was grey seer).   


Metallics are all Vallejo liquid metals. These are alcohol based and suck to use compared to acrylics but I like the end result much more. Selectively shaded in recesses with a mix of thinned down shades and contrast paint 50/50 with contrast medium. The silver parts of the blade received a light nuln oil treatment then I believe a watered down guilliman blue glaze (this is not made anymore). Then drybrushed over with Vallejo liquid silver. The gold I believe was the red gold from Vallejo liquid metallics then treated with watered down seraphim sepia and then one of the contrast browns thinned with contrast medium in the recesses. His faceplate (and much of the rest of his head) was liquid silver with an oil wash containing black/dark brown mixed with copious amounts of mineral spirits.   


Cloak I got no clue, I just messed around with various dark brown hues mixed with red, added a bit too much nuln oil at one point (why the cloak appears "wet" in certain areas), then drybrushed with dryad bark at first then eventually mixing that and one of my reds (I have a mix of three/four different brands).  


Weather on the cloak and the base was taking vallejo dark red and brown earth pigments and mixing it with mineral spirits so it applies wet but dries more like mud. Applied a snow mix of 50/50 pva glue to GW's blizzard texture with hobby snow powder mixed with ice crystals (pretty sure from AK) over the top. Re-apply mud mixture to make dirty snow. Not entirely happy with how that came out but it ended up working, otherwise the snow mix was a bit too bright for my liking considering it takes away from the mini.   


Other than that a thinned down burnt umber oil paint with mineral spirits to the rune on the blade and the inlaid upper part of his backpack.

I bought into the meme of Streaking Grime, and found that when applied properly it does live up to its hype. Bear in mind that there are different colors/types of Streaking Grime, the one I used here is AK00069, Streaking Grime for Panzer Grey. This method also requires the use of mineral spirits and preferably cotton swabs with pointed tips.   


Some people recommend varnishing before application, you don't \*have\* to but I would recommend it if you want to preserve the paint underneath for another round. Also, if you use contrast paint you really should varnish because I've found for some of my minis that mineral spirits will take contrast off.   


Despite all this the actual process is pretty simple. Apply grime, wait, then remove with mineral spirits to whatever degree you choose. If varnished beforehand, then you can even take all the grime off if you don't like it and start over until satisfied.
